commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Eve; implement greet-and-exit
commitResults.messageBody:
- Rename Duke.java to Eve.java; update ASCII banner to spell EVE
- Print greeting/farewell messages wrapped in divider lines, per the
  'greet the user and exit' requirement
- Update README.md and docs/README.md references from Duke to Eve

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Fill in student profile experience levels
commitResults.messageBody:
Set programming experience and IDE expertise to Intermediate instead
of the placeholder [to be filled] values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement command echo with exit on 'bye'
commitResults.messageBody:
- Read user input in a loop via Scanner
- Echo each command back wrapped in divider lines
- On 'bye', print farewell message and exit the loop

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to store and list tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
- Store user input in a fixed-size array (max 100 tasks)
  - 'list' command displays stored tasks with 1-based numbering
  - Non-command input now confirms storage via 'added: <task>'
    instead of just echoing it back

commitResults.messageTitle: Add present-changes-visually project skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Adapted from se-edu/skill-present-changes-visually (originally a Codex
skill) into a Claude Code project skill under .claude/skills/. It
generates a self-contained, GitHub-style split-view HTML diff of Git
changes (default: HEAD vs. worktree), using only Python's standard
library. Skill path updated from .codex/skills/ to .claude/skills/,
and the dangling reference to an upstream craft-commit-message skill
was replaced with an inline commit-message instruction since that
skill isn't part of this project.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command to update task status
commitResults.messageBody:
- Track done-status per task with a parallel boolean array
- 'list' now shows a [X]/[ ] status icon per task
- 'mark <n>' marks the n-th task as done and confirms it

commitResults.messageTitle: Add unmark command to reverse task done-status
commitResults.messageBody: - 'unmark <n>' marks the n-th task as not done and confirms it

commitResults.messageTitle: - Move description/done-status and their behavior into a new Task   class (src/main/java/Task.java); Eve.java now stores Task[] instead   of raw strings, calling markAsDone()/markAsNotDone()/getStatusIcon()
Fix Task.java: commit the real implementation
commitResults.messageBody:
The A-Classes commit (e62a88e) accidentally committed IntelliJ's empty
"New Class" stub (package PACKAGE_NAME; public class Task {}) instead
of the actual Task implementation, which only existed uncommitted in
the working tree. HEAD did not compile as a result, since Eve.java
already referenced Task's real fields/methods. This commits the real
class: description/isDone fields, constructor, getStatusIcon(),
getDescription(), markAsDone(), markAsNotDone().

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill for automated UI testing
commitResults.messageBody:
- New project skill (.claude/skills/test-ui/): compiles the program,
  runs every case in test/ui-test-plan.md against it (stdin in,
  stdout compared exactly), prints the session transcript, and stops
  immediately on the first failure with actual-vs-expected output.
  Standard-library-only Python, no packages to install.
- test/ui-test-plan.md: initial test cases covering greet+exit,
  add/list, mark, and unmark, each with an aim, input, and verified
  expected output.
- AGENTS.md: after any source change, update the test plan if needed
  and invoke the test-ui skill before proceeding (e.g. to committing).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ToDo, Deadline, and Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
- New ToDo/Deadline/Event classes extend Task, each overriding
  toString() to add its own type icon ([T]/[D]/[E]) and, for
  Deadline/Event, a "(by: ...)"/"(from: ... to: ...)" suffix; dates
  and times stay plain strings, unparsed, per the requirement
- Remove Task.getDescription(), now unused since list/mark/unmark
  display tasks via the new polymorphic toString() instead of
  manually rebuilding the status+description string
- Add 'todo', 'deadline', and 'event' commands to Eve.java, each
  parsing its command syntax (/by, /from, /to) and printing the
  "Got it. I've added this task" confirmation with the running count
- test/ui-test-plan.md: add test cases for todo/deadline/event and a
  mixed/marked case matching the requirement's example transcript;
  all 8 cases (4 existing + 4 new) verified via the test-ui skill

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle errors with a custom EveException (A-Exceptions)
commitResults.messageBody:
- New EveException (checked, extends Exception) represents chatbot-
  specific errors, per the A-Exceptions requirement
- Wrap the command loop in try/catch: todo/deadline/event reject
  empty or missing description, missing '/by', or missing/misordered
  '/from'+'/to'; mark/unmark (via a shared parseTaskNumber helper)
  reject a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range task number
- Replace the old catch-all, which silently added any text as a
  plain task, with a "don't know what that means" error -- implied
  by the 'blah' example, which has the same shape as that old
  free-text add
- test/ui-test-plan.md: update Tests 2-4 (relied on the retired
  free-text add) to use 'todo ', and add Tests 9-10 covering the
  requirement's own example plus malformed deadline/event and bad
  task numbers; all 10 cases verified via the test-ui skill

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command to remove tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
- 'delete <n>' removes the n-th task, confirming with the removed
  task's own display text and the updated count, shifting later
  tasks left by one to close the gap in the array
- Reuses parseTaskNumber() from Level 5, so missing, non-numeric, and
  out-of-range task numbers already get the same specific errors as
  mark/unmark with no new validation code needed
- test/ui-test-plan.md: add Test 11 (matches the requirement's own
  example transcript) and Test 12 (delete-specific error cases);
  all 12 cases verified via the test-ui skill

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a Command enum for command dispatch (A-Enums)
commitResults.messageBody:
- New Command enum (BYE/LIST/MARK/UNMARK/TODO/DEADLINE/EVENT/DELETE)
  replaces the string-prefix if/else chain with an enum switch --
  the natural fit here, since command words are a small, fixed,
  known set. Task types ([T]/[D]/[E]) stay as Task subclasses rather
  than an enum, since each needs different instance fields (by,
  from/to) that enum constants can't naturally carry per task
- Command.fromWord() maps an unrecognized word straight to the
  existing "don't know what that means" EveException, replacing the
  old catch-all else branch
- Eve.java now splits input into commandWord/arguments once up
  front, so every command handles a missing argument uniformly
  (todo no longer needs its old startsWith("todo ") special case)
- Side effect: command words are now case-insensitive (e.g. "Bye"
  works same as "bye"), since valueOf() is matched via toUpperCase()
- No behavior regressions: all 12 existing test-ui cases pass
  unchanged

commitResults.messageTitle: Show available commands in the startup greeting
commitResults.messageBody:
- Fix Eve.java: restore closing braces for the catch block and while
  loop that a stray edit had dropped, breaking compilation
- Command gains a description field alongside usage, so each command
  can describe itself in one place
- Greeting prints a column-aligned command reference (usage padded to
  the widest entry, then its description), computed dynamically so
  it stays aligned as commands change; added blank lines around the
  ASCII art and the "What can I do for you?" line for readability
- test/ui-test-plan.md: update the shared greeting block across all
  12 test cases in one pass; all still pass

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc to all public classes and methods
commitResults.messageBody:
All 7 public classes/types (Command, Deadline, Eve, EveException,
Event, Task, ToDo) and all 16 public methods (constructors included)
now have Javadoc, well past the "at least half" requirement.

Verified with the actual javadoc tool rather than just visual
inspection, which caught a real issue: a "<task number>" placeholder
inside a doc comment gets parsed as an HTML tag ("unknown tag: task")
-- fixed by wrapping it in {@code ...}. Remaining javadoc warnings are
just optional "no comment" nags for enum constants and protected
fields, which aren't public and don't count toward the requirement.

No behavior change: all 12 test-ui cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add toSaveFormat() to Task and its subclasses
commitResults.messageBody:
Teaches each task type to serialize itself to a pipe-delimited line
for Level 7's file persistence, mirroring the existing toString()
override pattern (each subclass adds its own type letter and extra
fields via super.toSaveFormat()):
  T | 1 | read book
  D | 0 | return book | June 6th
  E | 0 | project meeting | Aug 6th 2pm | 4pm
Not yet wired into Eve.java -- this commit only adds the capability.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load/save tasks from ./data/eve.txt (Level 7)
commitResults.messageBody:
- New Storage class: load() reads tasks from disk at startup,
  treating a missing file or missing data/ folder as an empty list
  rather than failing (handles first-run-on-a-new-machine); save()
  creates the data/ folder if needed and writes each task via its
  toSaveFormat(). Relative path built with Paths.get("data",
  "eve.txt") so it works the same on any OS.
- Corrupted-line handling (stretch goal): any line that doesn't
  parse -- wrong number of fields, unknown type letter, or a status
  field that isn't "0"/"1" -- is skipped with a warning instead of
  crashing the program or silently misreading it. Verified manually
  with a hand-edited data file mixing good and bad lines.
- Eve.java loads saved tasks into the array at startup, and calls
  Storage.save() after every command that mutates the list (todo,
  deadline, event, mark, unmark, delete); list/bye don't mutate, so
  they don't trigger a save.
- Note: the existing test-ui suite will fail until the runner is
  updated to reset data/eve.txt between test cases, since each test
  case now silently inherits whatever the previous one saved. That
  runner fix is a separate follow-up commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix test-ui isolation and add persistence test coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Level 7's automatic file persistence broke a hidden assumption in the
existing 12 test cases: each ran as an independent process, so none
referenced tasks from another test case, but once the program reads/
writes data/eve.txt, every new run auto-loads whatever the previous
run's process left behind -- silently corrupting unrelated tests.

- run_ui_tests.py: reset data/ before each test case's first run,
  restoring "every test case starts from a clean slate"; add two new
  test-plan capabilities needed to actually exercise persistence:
    - an optional second input/expected-output pair, run as a
      separate process invocation right after the first WITHOUT
      resetting data/ in between (proves data survives a real
      process restart, not just a code path)
    - an optional "Data file before run" block, written verbatim to
      the data file before the first run (lets a corrupted-file
      scenario be scripted and re-run automatically instead of only
      checked once by hand)
- SKILL.md: document both new formats.
- test/ui-test-plan.md: add Test 13 (tasks added/marked in one run
  are loaded by a second, separate run) and Test 14 (a data file
  with a garbage line and an invalid status field skips both with a
  warning, keeping the well-formed lines) -- automating the exact
  corrupted-line bug found and fixed while implementing Storage.

All 14 test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7: add task persistence (Level 7)
Understand dates and times for deadlines/events (Level 8)
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.by and Event.from/to are now java.time.LocalDate instead of
free-form String, per the Level 8 minimal requirement:
- Deadline/Event: parse/store as LocalDate; toString() displays via a
  DateTimeFormatter pinned to Locale.ENGLISH ("MMM d yyyy", e.g.
  "Dec 2 2019") so output is deterministic regardless of the host
  machine's default locale; toSaveFormat() writes LocalDate's own
  ISO toString() (e.g. "2019-12-02"), which is directly re-parseable.
- Eve.java: the DEADLINE/EVENT cases now call LocalDate.parse() on
  the /by, /from, /to text, catching DateTimeParseException and
  raising a field-specific EveException ("Please give the '/by' date
  as yyyy-mm-dd, e.g. ...") instead of silently accepting any text.
- Storage.java: parseLine() parses saved dates back with
  LocalDate.parse(); no new corruption handling needed --
  DateTimeParseException is already a RuntimeException, so it's
  caught by the existing corrupted-line machinery from Level 7 for
  free (verified: an old-format line with a free-text date is now
  correctly skipped with a warning instead of crashing).
- Command.java: usage strings updated to <yyyy-mm-dd> to guide users
  to the new format.
- test/ui-test-plan.md: updated every test's greeting block (command
  list column width changed) and every deadline/event input/expected
  output to use real dates instead of free text; added Test 15 for
  the new invalid-date rejection behavior, and folded the
  now-invalid old-format date into Test 14 as a third naturally
  occurring corrupted-line example. All 15 cases verified against
  the actual compiled program's output and pass.

Not implemented: LocalDateTime / time-of-day support (e.g. "2pm"),
which is the Level 8 stretch goal -- Minimal only calls for date-only
(yyyy-mm-dd) parsing, and the spec's own date-only event example
(orientation week) fits that scope cleanly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: understand dates and times (Level 8)
Add 'on <date>' to show tasks occurring on a date (Level 8 stretch)
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level 8 stretch goal: "add a command to print
deadlines/events occurring on a specific date."

- Task: add occursOn(LocalDate), default false since a plain to-do
  has no date to match against. Also move the DateTimeFormatter used
  for display up from Deadline/Event (which each had an identical
  private copy) into a shared public DISPLAY_FORMAT constant, so
  Eve.java can reuse it too.
- Deadline.occursOn(): true when the date equals its /by date.
- Event.occursOn(): true when the date falls within /from-/to
  inclusive (!isBefore && !isAfter), verified at both boundary dates
  and the day immediately outside each end.
- Command: new ON("on <yyyy-mm-dd>", ...) entry.
- Eve.java: new 'on' case -- validates the date (missing/invalid
  input gets a specific error, same pattern as deadline/event), then
  lists matching tasks renumbered from 1 within the filtered view,
  or prints a friendly "no tasks" message when nothing matches.
- test/ui-test-plan.md: updated the shared greeting block across all
  15 existing cases for the new command-list entry, and added
  Test 16 (matching/boundary/no-match/todo-excluded behavior) and
  Test 17 (missing/invalid date errors). All 17 cases verified
  against the actual compiled program's output and pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8-stretch: show tasks on a date (Level 8 stretch)
Extract Ui class (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
Move every console interaction (reading input, printing the greeting,
task confirmations, listings, and errors) out of Eve.java's main method
and into a new Ui class, so Eve is no longer responsible for exact
output formatting. Eve.java now just decides *what* to tell the user
(e.g. "a task was added") and hands the data to Ui, which decides *how*
to say it.

Behavior is unchanged (verified with test-ui: all 17 cases pass). This
is the first of four extractions toward A-MoreOOP's minimal target
(Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList); Storage/Parser/TaskList follow in
later commits on this branch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the raw Task[] tasks / int taskCount pair in Eve.java with a
TaskList that owns an ArrayList<Task> internally and exposes add/get/
delete/size, plus occurringOn(date) for the "on <date>" command. This
removes Eve's manual array shifting on delete and the fixed 100-task
capacity, and stops it from touching task storage internals directly.

Storage.save and Ui.showTaskList now take List<Task> instead of
Task[]/int, since TaskList exposes an unmodifiable view via asList()
rather than the backing array. Behavior is unchanged (test-ui: all 17
cases pass).

Second of four extractions toward A-MoreOOP's minimal target (Ui done
previously; Parser and an instance-based Storage remain).

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Storage an instance class bound to a file path (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage now matches the target design: new Storage(filePath) rather
than static load()/save() hardcoded to data/eve.txt. This makes the
file location a constructor parameter instead of a compile-time
constant, so it's no longer baked into the class.

load() now throws EveException when the file exists but can't be
read (previously it swallowed the IOException and printed a warning
directly). Eve.java catches that in its constructor-equivalent setup
step and calls the new Ui.showLoadingError(), falling back to an
empty TaskList -- matching the try/catch shape shown in the A-MoreOOP
spec's example Duke(String filePath) constructor. The "file doesn't
exist yet" and "corrupted line" cases are unchanged (still silent /
per-line warnings respectively), since both are already covered by
existing test-ui cases.

Behavior verified unchanged for the tested paths: test-ui, all 17
cases pass.

Third of four extractions toward A-MoreOOP's minimal target (Ui,
TaskList done previously). Parser is the remaining piece.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class (A-MoreOOP minimal target complete)
commitResults.messageBody:
Move command-word/argument splitting and all per-command argument
validation and date parsing out of Eve.java's main method into a new
Parser class. Each add-command's parse method (parseTodo,
parseDeadline, parseEvent) now returns a fully constructed Task, and
parseOnDate/parseTaskNumber return the parsed value directly -- so
Eve.java's switch cases are reduced to "parse, act on TaskList/
Storage, tell Ui", with no string manipulation or date-format logic
of its own.

Eve.java is now ~100 lines (down from ~260 originally) and reads as
a thin dispatcher, matching the shape shown in the A-MoreOOP spec's
example. Behavior is unchanged: test-ui, all 17 cases pass.

This completes A-MoreOOP's minimal target: Ui, Storage, Parser, and
TaskList are all extracted. The stretch goal (Command class hierarchy
with execute(tasks, ui, storage)) is still open.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Command class hierarchy (A-MoreOOP stretch goal)
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce an abstract Command with execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and
isExit(), and one concrete subclass per action: AddCommand,
ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, OnCommand,
ExitCommand. Parser.parse(fullCommand) now returns a ready-to-run
Command instead of Eve.java switching on a command-word enum and
inlining each action itself, so Eve.java's main loop is just:

  Command command = Parser.parse(fullCommand);
  command.execute(tasks, ui, storage);
  isExit = command.isExit();

matching the shape from the assignment's example run() method. Eve.java
is now ~35 lines.

Renamed the old command-word enum from Command to CommandWord, since
it's a different concept (known words + their usage/description text
for the welcome banner) from the new Command class hierarchy (executable
actions). Parser.parse uses CommandWord.fromWord to validate the typed
word and pick which Command subclass to build.

Mark/Unmark/Delete previously validated a task number's range (1..size)
at parse time using the current task count. Since Parser.parse no longer
has access to the TaskList (matching the spec's Parser.parse(fullCommand)
signature), that range check moved to a new TaskList.toIndex(taskNumber),
called from each command's execute(). Parser still catches the purely
syntactic errors (missing/non-numeric) before a Command is even built.
Error wording and triggering conditions are unchanged.

Kept line-bordering (the "____" divider before/after each message)
inside each Ui.showXxx method rather than centralizing it in the main
loop's finally block as the example sketches -- centralizing it would
have given "bye" a leading divider it doesn't have today, breaking the
existing, deliberately-tested output format. Behavior is otherwise
identical: test-ui, all 17 cases pass.

This completes A-MoreOOP, including the stretch goal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreOOP: extract Ui, TaskList, Storage, Parser, Command (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
Restructures the chatbot from a single ~260-line Eve.main into
cooperating classes: Ui (all console I/O), TaskList (the task
collection and its operations), Storage (load/save, now an instance
bound to a file path), Parser (turns a line of input into a Command),
and a Command hierarchy (AddCommand, ListCommand, MarkCommand,
UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, OnCommand, ExitCommand) executed via
Command.execute(tasks, ui, storage). Eve.main is now a ~35-line loop.

Meets both the minimal target and the stretch goal. Verified with
test-ui after every step; all 17 cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move all classes into the eve package (A-Packages minimal target)
commitResults.messageBody:
Move every class from src/main/java (the default/unnamed package) into
src/main/java/eve, and add "package eve;" to each file. src/main/java
stays the source root, as required -- only the package folder is new.

Update the test-ui runner (.claude/skills/test-ui/scripts/run_ui_tests.py)
to compile sources recursively (glob **/*.java instead of *.java) and
to run the entry class as eve.Eve instead of Eve.

No behavior change: test-ui, all 17 cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split into eve.task and eve.command sub-packages (A-Packages stretch goal)
commitResults.messageBody:
With 18 classes now in one flat eve package, group the two largest
natural clusters into their own sub-packages:

- eve.task: Task, ToDo, Deadline, Event, TaskList -- the task
  representation and the collection operations on it.
- eve.command: Command, CommandWord, AddCommand, ListCommand,
  MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, OnCommand, ExitCommand --
  the executable-command hierarchy and its supporting word lookup.

Eve, EveException, Parser, Storage, and Ui stay in the base eve
package: none of them has enough siblings to justify its own package,
and each is already a single well-defined responsibility.

Added explicit imports (no wildcard imports) at each cross-package
reference. src/main/java is still the source root.

No behavior change: test-ui, all 17 cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Packages: organize classes into packages (A-Packages)
commitResults.messageBody:
Moves every class out of the default package into eve (minimal
target), then splits the task and command classes into eve.task and
eve.command sub-packages as the class count grew (stretch goal).
src/main/java remains the source root. Also updates the test-ui
runner to compile recursively and run the entry class as eve.Eve.

Verified with test-ui after each step; all 17 cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge add-gradle-support: bring in Gradle wrapper and build.gradle (A-Gradle step 1)
commitResults.messageBody:
Per the A-Gradle instructions, merges the add-gradle-support branch
(provided upstream) to bring in the Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradlew.bat,

commitResults.messageTitle: Point Gradle at eve.Eve and add build instructions (A-Gradle complete)
commitResults.messageBody:
The merged-in build.gradle still targeted the template's
seedu.duke.Duke and shipped a "duke.jar" output name. Update
application.mainClass to eve.Eve (our actual entry point after
A-Packages) and rename the shadowJar output to eve.jar to match.

Also fix a stale path in README.md (src/main/java/Eve.java ->
src/main/java/eve/Eve.java, missed when A-Packages moved it) and add

`java -jar build/libs/eve.jar` both produce identical output to the

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Gradle: add Gradle build support (A-Gradle)
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges in the upstream add-gradle-support branch (Gradle wrapper +
starter build.gradle), then points application.mainClass at eve.Eve
and renames the shadowJar output to eve.jar to match this project.
Chatbot can now be built and run with `./gradlew run`, and packaged

in build.gradle for the upcoming A-JUnit increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Event and TaskList (A-JUnit minimal target)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add src/test/java/eve/task/EventTest.java and TaskListTest.java,
using the JUnit 5 dependencies already wired up in build.gradle
(from A-Gradle). Run via Gradle per the course's guidance to prefer
Gradle over the IDE runner from A-Gradle onward.

Covers two non-trivial methods from two different classes, reasonably
thoroughly:
- Event.occursOn(LocalDate): boundary conditions (day before/at/inside/
  at end/after the from-to range, plus a single-day event).
- TaskList.occurringOn(LocalDate) and TaskList.toIndex(int): mixed
  task-type filtering (ToDo never matches, Deadline/Event do), the
  empty-list and no-match cases, and every out-of-range case for
  toIndex (zero, negative, past the end, empty list), including the
  exact error message content.

Deliberately did not attempt the stretch goal (testing every
non-trivial public method of every class) in this pass: Ui, Storage,
and the Command classes all have I/O or cross-object collaboration
that would need test doubles/refactoring to test cleanly, which is a
separate, larger effort from the minimal target.

Verified: `./gradlew test` -- all 13 new test methods pass. The
existing test-ui suite (javac-based, unaffected by this change) still
passes all 17 cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-JUnit: add JUnit tests for Event and TaskList (A-JUnit)
commitResults.messageBody:
Meets A-JUnit's minimal target: at least two non-trivial methods from
two different classes, tested reasonably thoroughly (boundary
conditions, exception paths, and exact error messages), run via
Gradle per the course's A-Gradle-onward guidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword (Level 9)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `find <keyword>` to list every task whose description contains
the keyword (case-insensitive), matching the requirement's example
transcript exactly.

- Task.matches(keyword): case-insensitive substring check on the
  description, shared by all task types since none override it.
- TaskList.matching(keyword): filters to matches, mirroring the
  existing occurringOn(date) pattern.
- CommandWord.FIND + Parser.parseFindKeyword: rejects an empty
  keyword with a specific error, same style as the other commands.
- FindCommand: new Command subclass, executes the search and reports
  via the new Ui.showMatchingTasks (which also prints a friendly
  "no matching tasks" message when nothing matches).

Updated test/ui-test-plan.md: inserted the new "find <keyword>" line
into the welcome banner expected by all 17 existing cases (verified
the exact new banner by running the program manually first), and
added two new cases (find across mixed task types incl. a no-match
keyword, and find with a missing keyword).

Verified: test-ui, all 19 cases pass; `./gradlew test` still passes
the existing JUnit suite.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc to Storage.parseLine (A-JavaDoc)
commitResults.messageBody:
Audited every class for Javadoc coverage against A-JavaDoc's
requirements. Every non-private class and method already has a
header comment, carried forward from AGENTS.md's standing instruction
to document classes and nontrivial methods throughout the project --
this already meets the stretch goal (all non-trivial public methods
of all classes), not just the minimal target.

The one real gap was Storage.parseLine: a non-trivial private method
(parses one save-file line into a Task, or null with a warning if the
line is corrupted) that had no doc comment. Added one, completing the
stretch goal's "non-trivial private methods" clause too.

Verified: test-ui, all 17 cases pass (doc-only change).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
We don't yet have a reusable reference for the SE-EDU intermediate
Java conventions (https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html)
that this project needs to follow going forward (A-CodingStandard).

Add it as a project skill covering naming, layout/formatting,

reviewing Java code in this repo instead of relying on memory.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Same gap as the Java coding standard: no reusable reference existed
for the SE-EDU Git conventions (https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html)
that commit messages in this project should follow (A-CodingStandard).

Add it as a project skill covering subject-line rules, body structure,
and branch naming, so commit messages can be checked against it before
committing instead of relying on memory.

commitResults.messageBody:
The two SE-EDU convention skills just added (seedu-java-coding-standard,
seedu-git-standard) aren't useful unless something requires them to
actually be used.

Add mandates under "Project-specific requirements" pointing at each
skill: all Java code written or edited must follow the coding
standard, and every commit message must follow the Git standard.
